title: Worst places: Whiting, Indiana, and an insult in Florida
summary: Punch describes Whiting and a Florida insult.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, what's the worst place you ever been in? I think the worst place I've been in my life is waiting in Indiana.

Worse than Georgia, Mississippi? They're going right. You couldn't, you didn't have to hire an automobile or nothing in Georgia or Mississippi to go through there. They might get after you or something, but you didn't have to hire. But in Whitings, Indiana, if you was in an automobile, and any kind of white man in there, you'd have to hire. Get out in there and hire and do something to go through there. Whitings was just that bad in them times. And they said, just that way of yet. The boy was talking about it yesterday. They're just that bad right now. Whitings, Indiana. Well, what would they do to you? And they ain't got a near-color family that live there, near one. They can work there, but they gotta get on away from there.
What about, what would they do to you in Georgia, Mississippi? Do you have any experiences with them?

Well, no, I'm gonna tell you the truth. No, because I've never had no trouble in places. I always was, you know, stayed where I was supposed to stay and kept in the right places, you know, where I was belonging. I never did mingle up in places where I had no business, you know what I mean? I was telling them one insult I remember getting one time, that was in Florida though. I was expecting a letter from this fellow I used to work with, McBride. And, you know, I told him just write to the post office and I'd go get it. And I went there to ask for a meal. And some white guy asked me, nigga, where are you going? I told him I'd come to ask for a meal. here. I said, well you just wait there and tell this white people get from around here and then you come on in, we'll let you on in. Well that's the only place I've had any trouble. They didn't do me nothing, but that's just the way they spoke to me, you know.
